text:
maria: Seeing a bunch of GPU pod evictions right after the nightly scaledown. Lots of small leftover jobs that fragment nodes, scheduler struggles to pack new realtime pods. anyone else? :thinking:

akshay: saw the same in cluster-west-2. Pod pending -> preempted chain, then burst of evictions. Noticed a lot of pods with tolerations but no nodeAffinity, so they float.

ev‎an: logs look like binpacking score oscillation. Scheduler schedules by free-memory then k8s preemption kicks in because of priority class mismatch.
lucy: heap: we reduced node counts to save cost so fragmentation visible now. can we do a cheap fix like preferAvoid or topologySpread?

akshay: preferAvoid won't help if pods don't express constraints. we could try: set a soft nodeAffinity to prefer packing on nodes with label "gpu-shard=true" and then slowly roll it out. example: `preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution` with weight 50.
maria: +1 on soft affinity. also think we should mark low-priority batch pods with `reclaimable=true` label and run a small ClusterAutoscaler tweak to evict them first.
sre-bot: incident:gpu-frag-2026 created by maria at 2026-03-18T09:28:xxZ. Current severity: P2. Affected: realtime-serving, batch-ml.
ev‎an: another angle: kernel of problem is mixed-instance types in same AZ causing weird packing (v100+rtx in same node pool). Proposal: split nodepools by GPU type and add pod tolerations to target them. fewer cross-packing decisions.
lucy: downside is less flexible binpacking -> potential idle GPUs. But we can run a small defrag job that consolidates reclaimable pods at 03:00 UTC and free full nodes for realtime.
akshay: defrag job idea: cronjob that uses `kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --force` on nodes with label `defrag-candidate=true` after cordoning them with `NoSchedule`. We'll need to be careful with PDBs.
maria: agree on PDB caution. also worth experimenting with scheduler plugin scoring: increase gpu-utilization-weight and add a fragmentation-penalty function so nodes with many small allocs get negative score.
ev‎an: i can prototype a kube-scheduler extender that adds penalty based on `gpu.alloc_chunks` annotation. lightweight PoC this week.
lucy: timeline? ops needs a safe rollback plan. if we change scoring, ensure canary in dev cluster and run soak for 48h.
maria: ok let's do canary in west-2-dev tonight. evan, akshay — coordinate. I'll add a runbook and a patch to autoscaler to treat `reclaimable=true` as first-evict.
akshay: pinging @evan for access to west-2-dev. also will add a Prom alert for "gpu_fragmentation_ratio > 0.35" to detect earlier.
sre-bot: uptime-check scheduled: canary-west-2-dev starting 2026-03-18T23:00Z. Will post results in this thread. :rocket:
maria: thanks all. small action items: (1) evan prototype scheduler plugin, (2) akshay autoscaler change + alert, (3) lucy orchestrate defrag cronjob and PDB audit. followups here after canary. :thumbsup:
